scope: tcHandleWallet finite response/body verification wait and timeout feedback
assessment: Promise.race covers both fetch and JSON body parsing. The timeout marks expired before abort; an explicit expired guard prevents a simultaneously resolved body from applying success.

Completion-time clock guard additionally rejects elapsed time >=8 seconds or wall-clock rollback before any recipient application, even when hidden-tab timer delivery is delayed. It marks expired and aborts before throwing into current-only timeout feedback.

The losing response operation only produces data; it has no recipient mutation, UI message, pending release or timer cleanup. Its later resolution/rejection cannot apply an obsolete address or affect a new verification.

Single outer finally clears the timer and releases tcPending after timeout, allowing a new explicit preparation. Consumed persistent connection intent and recipient-state guards remain intact; stale timeout feedback is suppressed.
Current timeout feedback reports excessive wait and manual/explicit reconnect options. It does not claim server cancellation or absent wallet association.

Backend verify endpoint remembers a successfully verified wallet association before returning its response; browser timeout or abort does not cancel or order this server-side profile write. This UI-only recovery does not change backend association semantics.
Only tcHandleWallet changes; verification request body, strict success checks, preparation/intent machinery, other form flows and backend untouched.
Read-only production preflight passed with 58 live inputs and 4 unchanged services. Seventeen local scope/drift/atomic apply/reconcile/rollback checks passed.

backend_limit.description: Successful verification may still update the profile wallet association even when its response arrives after browser timeout; no cancellation guarantee is made.
